purpose: Reviewed conceptual system illustrations; quantitative plots are regenerated from data by Python.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a NEW original publication-ready EvoHarness architecture figure. Attached images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: AlphaEvolve Figure 2 and KernelBench Figure 1. Learn their compact scientific visual grammar, clear component boundaries, labeled data arrows, short labels, code artifact cards, distinct evaluation modules. Do not copy their content, layout verbatim, paper page text, brands or captions. This figure must look like a high-end ML systems paper, not a corporate slide, numbered six-column infographic, poster, or marketing diagram.

Canvas: wide landscape 2:1, clean white. Flat vector-like graphics, thin dark outlines, restrained pastel blue for agent/controller, pale teal for sandbox physics, pale gold for validation, pale plum for evidence. Crisp sans-serif labels and a little monospaced code. No large title banner, no shadows, no gradients, no 3D container ship icons, no slogan, no decorative network art. Short exact labels only, generous whitespace and precise directional arrows.

Build a single integrated system with two visibly nested loops and one optional sidebar:
Upper left small input block "Experiment contract" with three tiny lines "task + seed origin", "model + budget", "enabled mechanisms". Arrow into left-center "Context assembly". Under Context assembly a small "Optional memory" notebook icon and "Curated knowledge" card feed into it.
Across upper-middle: Context assembly -> rounded "LLM proposer" -> code document "Candidate program" displaying only "def solve(fm, rng):" and "    return boundary".
Across right-middle a large teal dashed enclosure with heading "Offline evaluation sandbox". The code document enters this enclosure. INSIDE it two modules form an inner loop: "Candidate optimizer" on the left and "VMEC++ forward model" on the right. Arrow from optimizer to forward model labeled "boundary parameters"; return arrow from forward model to optimizer labeled "metrics / optional gradients". Include a small wireframe toroidal stellarator surface next to forward model, only as a conceptual geometry glyph. Label inside enclosure bottom "Metered calls · CPU · memory · no network".
A boundary artifact leaves sandbox downward via arrow labeled "returned boundary", into a SEPARATE gold module "Clean re-score" with subtitle "candidate code removed". From Clean re-score an arrow points LEFT to gold "Evaluation record" containing three short rows "score + constraints", "fidelity + failures", "origin + fingerprint".
From Evaluation record LEFT into lower-center purple "Selection + archive" with database icon. Short subtitle "policy depends on workflow". A large LEFT-and-UP return arrow from Selection + archive into Context assembly is labeled "parents + measured feedback". This is the outer loop and must be visibly cyclic. A secondary arrow from Evaluation record to "Append-only ledger" document at bottom carries all attempts, including rejection.
Small far-right neutral dashed sidebar labeled "Optional research DAG": "Coordinator → workers → referee". Use a dashed connection to Experiment contract or candidate proposals, clearly separate, never mandatory.
Bottom mini-strip with three gates: "VLF screen → LF confirm → Official evaluation", caption "Structural promotion path".
Small bottom-left tag "(a) Agent search / (b) Inner physics / (c) Verification".

Scientific constraints: LLM weights are fixed; do not draw weight training. Inner optimizer changes boundaries, outer loop changes code/context. Official validation is same pinned solver stack in a fresh container, NOT independent scientific replication. Do not label a result successful or add checkmarks implying this repo has found a feasible independent stellarator. No numeric results. Do not add invented code, hidden new modules, duplicated stages, marketing text, or any extra slogans. Arrows must preserve the specified directions. All words correctly spelled and legible at README width.
edits:
Edit this EvoHarness paper-style architecture diagram with three precise corrections only, preserving all other text, layout, colors, icons, geometry, and component positions:
1. Replace the top dashed-line label "optional distributed execution" with the exact label "optional research orchestration".
2. Inside the teal sandbox, the lower arrow labeled "metrics / optional gradients" must point ONLY LEFT, from the VMEC++ forward model back to Candidate optimizer. Remove its rightward arrowhead; retain the upper rightward "boundary parameters" arrow.
3. In the VMEC++ module, arrange the small toroidal wireframe glyph above the label or in a non-overlapping corner, so "VMEC++ forward model" is completely legible with no geometry drawn through the words.
Do not introduce any new words, slogans, performance claims, stages, effects, or decorations. Keep the clean flat scientific systems-paper visual style.

Make a minimal correction to this existing diagram; preserve everything else exactly. The candidate code must read "def solve(fm, rng):" (f followed by lowercase m, not n), followed by "return boundary". In the sandbox there are two horizontal arrows. Keep the UPPER arrow right-pointing (boundary parameters). Replace the LOWER double-headed horizontal arrow with this single arrow shape: ← . The lower arrow has its arrowhead at the LEFT beside Candidate optimizer and a plain line ending on the RIGHT beside VMEC++; no right arrowhead. The label under it remains "metrics / optional gradients". Do not change any layout, other text, colors or icons.

Correct one scientific detail in this existing EvoHarness architecture figure, preserving its overall layout and visual style. Training feedback can reach selection before a separate validation run; not every candidate receives official verification. Add a clearly labeled direct arrow from the LOWER-LEFT edge of the teal "Offline evaluation sandbox" to the TOP-RIGHT edge of the gold "Evaluation record" box. Route it through the existing white gap without crossing text. Label this new arrow "train feedback". Keep the existing path from sandbox down to clean re-score and then left into Evaluation record. Rename the clean re-score box to "Clean validation"; its subtitle must be "val / official; code removed". This now makes two distinct paths visible: direct training feedback and separate clean validation. Keep "def solve(fm, rng):" exact. Keep the optional research DAG, memory, all other modules, colors, wording, and positions unchanged. Do not introduce additional modules or decorations.

assets.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset: sophisticated wide landscape research architecture illustration for EvoHarness README. Create an exploded layered systems diagram titled "What the optimizer learns — and what it controls". White background, navy typography, restrained blue teal purple amber accents, subtle depth with semi-isometric plates, publication-quality science design. Six stacked architectural layers, with clean straight routing lines and concise readable text. From top to bottom exact layer labels and content: "01  Experiment contract" / "Task · models · budgets · provenance"; "02  Model proposal" / "Fixed LLM weights · evolving programs"; "03  Search and selection" / "Greedy · islands · staged · bandit forks"; "04  Context and feedback" / "Scores · reflections · reviewed memory · task notes"; "05  Task evaluation" / "Bin packing · circles · TSP · C kernels · CVRP · stellarators"; "06  Execution and evidence" / "Isolation · fidelity · ledgers · verification". A clear side feedback loop rises from layer 06 to layer 02, labeled "Measured outcomes guide the next proposal". Add a distinct small dashed side panel labeled "Optional research orchestration" with "Coordinator → workers → referee" and "Dependent tasks + artifact evidence"; connect by a dashed arrow to the experimental contract, not a mandatory stage of each run. At the bottom in a calm note exact text "Programs, context, and archives evolve. Model weights are not updated." Include a small stylized network glyph inside the model layer and six minimalist task pictograms in evaluation layer, including a toroidal stellarator. This must visually clarify software layers and the control loop, not pretend to show a neural-network training architecture. Do not add numerical performance claims or tables with invented data. Beautiful typographic hierarchy, lots of whitespace, readable at README width, high-resolution landscape 16:9.
